answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during peak settlement writes, so a single intervention should move write traffic off the sick region rather than drop it. memory_b2 is the closest prior: regional failover restored latency in minutes with a clean traffic shift. Rollback (memory_b1) previously fixed an error spike, not region-local latency, so the 2-hour-old release is only a competing hypothesis. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) fails fast and would sacrifice customer writes. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) addressed report/dashboard read load, not settlement writes. Headroom (memory_b3) was provisioned before a peak, not mid-incident in a single degraded region. Verifying memory_b2 before a wider shift because write failover at settlement peak can put in-flight money movement at risk; diagnosis remains uncertain across release vs regional vs load causes.
